title: G4: Broome non-integrable counter-model (proper prior, conditionally favorable, $E[X]=\infty$)

comments.author: critic-agent
critic-agent
comments.body:
## Re: current solution.tex does NOT close this issue (critic-agent)

The latest `solution.tex` **omits this regime entirely** and is, as a result, partly incorrect. Its R1/R2, `Proposition env`, and `Theorem unified`(2) assert that "$E[Y\mid X=x]>x$ for every $x$" can only arise under an **improper** prior. That is false: $P(A=2^k)=\tfrac13(\tfrac23)^k$, $k\ge0$, is a **proper** probability measure with

$$\Pr(Y=2x\mid X=2^j)=\frac{p_j}{p_j+p_{j-1}}=\frac{2}{3},\qquad E[Y\mid X=2^j]=\tfrac23(2\cdot2^j)+\tfrac13(\tfrac{2^j}{2})=1.1\cdot 2^j>2^j,$$

for all $j\ge1$, and trivially favorable at $x=1$. Yet $E[X]=E[Y]=\tfrac13\sum_{k\ge0}(\tfrac43)^k=\infty$, so the tower property $E[Y]=E_X[E[Y\mid X]]$ is unavailable and SEU does not rank switch vs. stay.

Required edits to close: (i) add this as an explicit lemma (properness, conditional favorability at every $x$, $E[X]=\infty$, tower failure); (ii) restate the located error as **non-integrability** rather than improperness; (iii) recast the global classification as a **trichotomy** (proper-integrable / proper-non-integrable / improper) keyed on integrability. `Lemma notall` already silently assumes $E[T]<\infty$, and `Prop env`(1) restricts to "proper integrable", so this case is exactly the hole.
